attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own Substack post, said in his own voice after citing the NYT item.

semantics.note: The proposition fits the context about edge cases and keeps the 'no matter how much data' qualifier. But 'always' and the unlimited training volume make it an ongoing claim about the future, not just an observation. The contract's forecast axis is the better fit, and the drafter's kind conflicts with it.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair: novel situations persist, and trivial variations don't count. The contract correctly says a finite list of incidents can't settle the unlimited claim. The result depends on how much difference counts as 'new', which the speaker never defined.

evidence.note: A 2024 arXiv preprint saying rare or unseen inputs are an ongoing problem for end-to-end models. It is consistent with the claim but does not show that novelty persists at any data volume.

A Feb 2026 Waymo company disclosure about using simulation to prepare for rare scenarios. It is not an independent finding, and it does not show that training can cover every future situation. Context only.

reviews.rationale: The claim is a firm, unlimited assertion with no deadline. Neither item shows that novelty persists at every training volume, and neither shows that training coverage can exhaust road situations. The early-resolution rule is not met, so the packet does not settle the outcome by the 2026-10-28 cutoff.
